newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Russia to sign gas deal despite criticism. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland, Russia to sign gas deal despite criticism. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]

text.p: Polish and Russian gas firms will sign a long-term natural gas delivery deal on Wednesday despite criticism it would expose Poland's energy sector to political risk in Russia, Industry Minister Klemens Scierski said.
The deal includes Russia's Gazprom and Polish Polskie Gornictwo Naftowe i Gazownictwo (PGNiG).
"Gazprom and PGNiG will sign a contract on the delivery of gas and the contract is a great opportunity for our economy," Scierski told a news briefing on Tuesday.
He said the deal concerned gas from a large pipeline that would link the Siberian peninsula of Yamal and Western Europe through Poland. The construction of the pipeline started early this year.

Scierski said that under the contract the first three billion (corrects from million) cubic metres of gas would flow to Poland in 1997 and the amount would be gradually increased to cover between 29 and 43 percent of Poland's needs in the year 2009, estimated at between 22 and 27 billion (corrects from million) cubic metres.
Scierski brushed off recent criticism that the contract would make Poland's energy sector vulnerable to political instability in Russia.
He said the Yamal pipeline would be a transit one and there was no possibility of cutting off deliveries only to Poland.
He said Poland would also build reserve tanks for about five billion cubic metres of gas within the next several years, which would cover Poland's gas consumption for up to 160 days.
